new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Only one work is listed for this item (Hatfield & McHenry 2011, marked silent), and it was checked in full by whole-text search, so no listed silent or unopened work remains to spot-check. As extra diligence the earlier-check files in the same folder that the compiler conflicts field relies on were a full-text search for stress/accent: 'accent' only as names of tone diacritics, pp. 66), 'accent' as diacritic names; 'phenomene accentuel' p. 88 refers to the HB melody imposed in verbal reduplication in Kotafon, not to word stress and not to Ayizo), MuyskenSmith2014 djvu text (15 'stress' hits, all the verb 'stress' or creole/English prosody; the Ayizo mentions are migration history only). Not…

sources.citation: Gbéto, Flavien. 2004. Esquisse de la tonologie synchronique du wemɛgbe, dialecte gbe du Sud-Bénin. Studies in African Linguistics 33(1): 65-90.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number Philol 895.5; Widener Library (offsite storage)); the library holds the journal volume but the item itself was not found; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number Philol 895.5; Widener Library (offsite storage)
sources.note: SISTER LECT Weme; the template of the 'Esquisse de la tonologie synchronique' series (consonants, syllable structures, method, verb tones, noun tones, analysis, conclusion). 'accent' occurs only as diacritic names (p. 66). No stress/accent section -- suggests the Ayizo article likely has none either, but unverified.

sources.citation: Muysken, Pieter & Norval Smith (eds.). 2014. Surviving the Middle Passage: The West Africa-Surinam Sprachbund (TiLSM 275). Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. OAPEN open access.
sources.note: Gbe migration/noun-class-prefix chapter mentions Ayizo (Allada, Glo) and 'Emigrant Ayizo' lects (Toli): prefix vowels only. All 'stress' hits concern Sranan/Jamaican/English. Nothing on Ayizo prosody.

sources.citation: Hatfield, Deborah H. & Michael M. McHenry. 2011. A sociolinguistic survey of the Gbe language communities of Benin and Togo, Volume 2: Ayizo language area. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2011-014. Dallas: SIL International.
sources.note: Open-access normally; its 'Previous linguistic research' section will name any CNL/CENALA or UNB maîtrise sketches of Ayizo phonology that no catalogue surfaced. Unreachable today only because sil.org blocks our network and the the Internet Archive was offline.

sources.citation: Kluge, Angela. 2011. A sociolinguistic survey of the Gbe language communities of Benin and Togo: Gbe language family overview. SIL ESR 2011-012; Kluge 2007 LD&C 1(2); Kluge 2008 SIL ESR 2008-023.
sources.note: Classification/lexicostatistics; Ayizo sampled as a Phla-Phera/Fon-cluster variety; 'stress' only as Kruskal MDS stress. Nothing on word stress.

sources.citation: Gbéto, Flavien. 2006. La participation des consonnes comme unités porteuses de ton en kotafon, dialecte gbe du Sud-Bénin. Journal of West African Languages 33(2): 87-107.
sources.note: SISTER LECT Kotafon, same author/year/template; cites the Ayizo JALL paper. Two underlying tones H and B, derived M/BH/HB/MH/HM; voiceless obstruents insert H. Only accent wording: intro p. 88 'une règle qui assigne la mélodie tonale HB, interprétation d'un phénomène accentuel en œuvre au niveau du redoublement des radicaux verbaux CcV dont C est voisée' and sec. 5.3 (replacive tone melody in verbal reduplication). No word-stress statement; nothing on Ayizo beyond the citation.

sources.citation: Gbéto, Flavien. 2004. Tonologie synchronique du tɔfingbe du village lacustre de Ganvié, dialecte gbe du Sud-Bénin. JWAL 31(2): 27-46.
sources.note: SISTER LECT Tofin, same template; 'accent' only as diacritic names; no word-stress statement (per sibling check and a full-text search for stress/accent).

fr: notes give two base tones H and B with derived M, BH, HB, MH, HM (wording matches Gbeto's abstracts) and a bibliography (Gbeto 2006 JALL; Agossou-Voyèmè local Cotonou publications; Capo; Kluge); en: orthographic tone marking only. Nothing on accent/stress.

sources.note: Settled as a PASSING MENTION, not a tone description: an ethnohistorical monograph (LC subjects Aja/Ewe history and genealogy) by a missionary grammarian (author of Ewe/Aja/Gen grammars 1972/1975 and a Gen dictionary 1981); its introductory survey of the Ajatado peoples (pp. ~18-24) contains one comparative tone statement, p. 24, known only through Hatfield & McHenry 2011 fn. 10: two tonal systems exist among the Gbe languages, Ayizo having a 'ton ponctuel' (level/register tones) and Fon a 'ton modulé' (contour tones). No tone inventory, rules or data for Ayizo are reported from it anywhere;…
